And the castes and stages of life will remain established in their own duties, O best of men;
thus in all cosmic ages and in all eras of Manus,

16.s:
avatārā asaṅkhyātā atītānāgatādayaḥ /
viṣṇordaśāvatārākhyān yaḥ paṭhet śṛṇuyānnaraḥ //
16.d:
अवतारा असङ्ख्याता अतीतानागतादयः /
विष्णोर्दशावताराख्यान् यः पठेत् शृणुयान्नरः //
16.m:
the incarnations are innumerable, past, future, and present.
A man who recites or hears the narrative of the ten incarnations of Viṣṇu,

16.s:
sovāptakāmo vimalaḥ sakulaḥ svargamāpnuyāt /
dharmādharmavyavasthānamevaṃ vai kurute hariḥ /
avatīrṇañca sa gataḥ sargādeḥ kāraṇaṃ hariḥ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye buddhakalkyavatāravarṇanaṃ nāma
ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
sṛṣṭiviṣayakavarnanam
16.d:
सोवाप्तकामो विमलः सकुलः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् /
धर्माधर्मव्यवस्थानमेवं वै कुरुते हरिः /
अवतीर्णञ्च स गतः सर्गादेः कारणं हरिः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये बुद्धकल्क्यवतारवर्णनं नाम
षोडशो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ सप्तदशो ऽध्यायः
सृष्टिविषयकवर्ननम्
16.m:
with his desires attained, purified, will attain heaven along with his family.
In this way indeed Hari establishes righteousness and unrighteousness;
having incarnated, he departed—Hari, the cause of creation and the rest.
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, entitled ‘The Description of the Incarnations of the Buddha and Kalki’, in the primary Mahāpurāṇa, the Āgneya.
Now the seventeenth chapter.
Description of creation.

17.s:
agnir uvāca
jagatsargādikān krīḍān viṣṇorvakṣyedhunā śṛṇu /
svargādikṛt sa sargādiḥ sṛṣṭyādiḥ saguṇoguṇaḥ //
:p 40
17.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
जगत्सर्गादिकान् क्रीडान् विष्णोर्वक्ष्येधुना शृणु /
स्वर्गादिकृत् स सर्गादिः सृष्ट्यादिः सगुणोगुणः //
:प् 40
17.m:
Agni said:
I shall now relate the play of Viṣṇu, such as the creation of the universe; listen:
he is the creator of heaven and the rest, the origin of creation and the rest, the cause of creation and the rest, endowed with qualities, [yet] devoid of qualities.
:p 40

17.s:
brahmāvyaktaṃ sadāgre 'bhūt na khaṃ rātridinādikaṃ /
prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ viṣṇuḥ(1) praviśyākṣobhayattataḥ //
17.d:
ब्रह्माव्यक्तं सदाग्रे ऽभूत् न खं रात्रिदिनादिकं /
प्रकृतिं पुरुषं विष्णुः(1) प्रविश्याक्षोभयत्ततः //
17.m:
In the beginning there was always the unmanifest Brahman, not space, nor night, day, and so forth.
Then Viṣṇu, having entered primordial matter and the conscious spirit, agitated [them].

17.s:
svargakāle mahattattvamahaṅkārastato 'bhavat /
vaikārikastaijasaś ca bhūtādiś caiva tāmasaḥ //
17.d:
स्वर्गकाले महत्तत्त्वमहङ्कारस्ततो ऽभवत् /
वैकारिकस्तैजसश् च भूतादिश् चैव तामसः //
17.m:
At the time of creation, the principle of cosmic intellect arose; from that came the ego-sense:
the modified, the fiery, and the elemental, which is dark.

From the ego-sense arose the subtle element of sound, and thence space;
from that, the subtle element of touch [and] wind; thence, the subtle element of form [and] fire;

17.s:
rasamātrā āpa ito gandhamātrā mahī smṛtā(2) /
ahaṅkārāttāmasāttu taijasānīndriyāṇi ca //
17.d:
रसमात्रा आप इतो गन्धमात्रा मही स्मृता(2) /
अहङ्कारात्तामसात्तु तैजसानीन्द्रियाणि च //
17.m:
hence the subtle element of taste [and] water; the subtle element of odor [and] earth is handed down.
From the dark ego-sense [arose the elements], and the fiery [produced] the senses;

17.s:
vaikārikā daśa devā mana ekādaśendriyam /
tataḥ svayaṃbhūrbhagavān(3) sisṛkṣurvividhāḥ prajāḥ //
17.d:
वैकारिका दश देवा मन एकादशेन्द्रियम् /
ततः स्वयंभूर्भगवान्(3) सिसृक्षुर्विविधाः प्रजाः //
17.m:
from the modified [ego-sense came] the ten deities, and mind is the eleventh sense.
Then the self-born Lord, desiring to create various creatures,

17.s:
apa eva sasarjādau tāsu vīryamavāsṛjat(4) /
āpo nārā iti proktā āpo vai narasūnavaḥ //
17.d:
अप एव ससर्जादौ तासु वीर्यमवासृजत्(4) /
आपो नारा इति प्रोक्ता आपो वै नरसूनवः //
17.m:
created the waters first of all, and cast his potency into them.
The waters are called nārāḥ, for the waters are indeed the sons of Nara.

17.s:
ayanantasya tāḥ pūrvantena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
hiraṇyavarṇamabhavat(5) tadaṇḍamudakeśayam //
17.d:
अयनन्तस्य ताः पूर्वन्तेन नारायणः स्मृतः /
हिरण्यवर्णमभवत्(5) तदण्डमुदकेशयम् //
17.m:
Formerly they were his abode; therefore he is remembered as Nārāyaṇa.
That egg, resting in the water, became golden in color.

17.s:
tasmin jajñe svayaṃ brahmā svayambhūriti naḥ śrutam /
hiraṇyagarbho(6) bhagavānuṣitvā parivatsaram //
17.d:
तस्मिन् जज्ञे स्वयं ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूरिति नः श्रुतम् /
हिरण्यगर्भो(6) भगवानुषित्वा परिवत्सरम् //
17.m:
In it Brahmā himself was born; he is known as the self-born, so we have heard.
The Lord Hiraṇyagarbha, having dwelt [there] for a full year,

17.s:
tadaṇḍamakarot dvaidhandivaṃ bhuvamathāpi ca /
tayoḥ śakalayormadhye ākāśamasṛjat prabhuḥ //
17.d:
तदण्डमकरोत् द्वैधन्दिवं भुवमथापि च /
तयोः शकलयोर्मध्ये आकाशमसृजत् प्रभुः //
17.m:
split that egg in two, into heaven and earth as well.
Between those two halves the Lord created space.

17.s:
apsu pāriplavāṃ pṛthivīṃ diśaś ca daśadhā dadhe /
tatra kālaṃ mano vācaṃ kāmaṃ krodhamatho ratim //
:n
1 viṣṇumiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 gandhamātrā dharitryabhūditi kha, ga, gha,
cihnitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
3 tataḥ svayambhūrbhagavānityārabhya sraṣṭumicchan
prajāpatirityantapāṭhastu mahābhāratīyaharivaṃśaparvaṇa uddhṛta
iti adhyavasīyate ubhayatra krameṇa pāṭhasāmyāt
4 tāsu bījamathāsṛjaditi kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 hiraṇyagarbhamabhavaditi kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
6 hiraṇyavarṇa iti ga, cihnitgapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 41
17.d:
अप्सु पारिप्लवां पृथिवीं दिशश् च दशधा दधे /
तत्र कालं मनो वाचं कामं क्रोधमथो रतिम् //
:न्
1 विष्णुमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 गन्धमात्रा धरित्र्यभूदिति ख, ग, घ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
3 ततः स्वयम्भूर्भगवानित्यारभ्य स्रष्टुमिच्छन्
प्रजापतिरित्यन्तपाठस्तु महाभारतीयहरिवंशपर्वण उद्धृत
इति अध्यवसीयते उभयत्र क्रमेण पाठसाम्यात्
4 तासु बीजमथासृजदिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 हिरण्यगर्भमभवदिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
6 हिरण्यवर्ण इति ग, चिह्नित्गपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 41
17.m:
He placed the earth floating upon the waters, and set out the directions tenfold;
there [he created] time, mind, speech, desire, anger, and pleasure.
:n
1 "viṣṇum" is the reading of the manuscript marked kha.
2 "gandhamātrā dharitryabhūt" is the reading of the three manuscripts marked kha, ga, and gha.
3 The text beginning from "tataḥ svayambhūrbhagavān" up to "sraṣṭumicchan prajāpatiḥ" is determined to be extracted from the Harivaṃśa section of the Mahābhārata, because the reading is identical in both in sequence.
4 "tāsu bījamathāsṛjat" is the reading of the manuscript marked kha.
5 "hiraṇyagarbhamabhavat" is the reading of the manuscript marked kha.
6 "hiraṇyavarṇaḥ" is the reading of the manuscript marked ga.
:p 41

17.s:
sasarja sṛṣṭintadrūpāṃ sraṣṭumicchan prajāpatiḥ /
vidyutośanimeghāṃś ca rohitendradhanūṃṣi ca //
17.d:
ससर्ज सृष्टिन्तद्रूपां स्रष्टुमिच्छन् प्रजापतिः /
विद्युतोशनिमेघांश् च रोहितेन्द्रधनूंषि च //
17.m:
Prajāpati, desiring to create, fashioned creation conforming to that nature:
lightning, thunderbolts, clouds, red rainbows, and Indra's bows,

17.s:
vayāṃsi ca sasarjādau parjanyañcātha vaktrataḥ /
ṛco yajūṃṣi sāmāni nirmame yajñasiddhaye //
17.d:
वयांसि च ससर्जादौ पर्जन्यञ्चाथ वक्त्रतः /
ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि निर्ममे यज्ञसिद्धये //
17.m:
and first he created birds, and then rain from his mouth.
He fashioned the verses of the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, and the Sāmaveda for the accomplishment of sacrifice.

17.s:
sādhyāstair ayajandevān bhūtamuccāvacaṃ bhujāt(1) /
sanatkumāraṃ rudrañca sasarja krodhasambhavam //
17.d:
साध्यास्तैर् अयजन्देवान् भूतमुच्चावचं भुजात्(1) /
सनत्कुमारं रुद्रञ्च ससर्ज क्रोधसम्भवम् //
17.m:
With them the Sādhyas sacrificed to the gods; and from his arm [arose] beings high and low.
He created Sanatkumāra, and Rudra, who was born of his anger;

17.s:
marīcimatryaṅgirasaṃ pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum /
vasiṣṭhaṃ mānasāḥ sapta brahmāṇa iti niścitāḥ(2) //
17.d:
मरीचिमत्र्यङ्गिरसं पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम् /
वसिष्ठं मानसाः सप्त ब्रह्माण इति निश्चिताः(2) //
17.m:
Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,
and Vasiṣṭha—these are determined to be the seven mind-born Brahmās.

17.s:
saptaite janayanti sma prajā rudrāś ca sattama /
dvidhā kṛtvātmano dehamardhena puruṣo 'bhavat //
ardhena nārī tasyāṃ sa brahmā vai cāsṛjat prajāḥ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye jagatsargavarṇanaṃ nāma saptadaśo
'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha aṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
svāyambhuvavaṃśavarṇanam
17.d:
सप्तैते जनयन्ति स्म प्रजा रुद्राश् च सत्तम /
द्विधा कृत्वात्मनो देहमर्धेन पुरुषो ऽभवत् //
अर्धेन नारी तस्यां स ब्रह्मा वै चासृजत् प्रजाः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये जगत्सर्गवर्णनं नाम सप्तदशो
ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ अष्टादशो ऽध्यायः
स्वायम्भुववंशवर्णनम्
17.m:
These seven engendered creatures, and the Rudras, O best of men.
Having divided his body into two, with one half he became a man,
and with one half a woman; upon her that Brahmā indeed begot creatures.
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, entitled ‘The Description of the Creation of the Universe’, in the primary Mahāpurāṇa, the Āgneya.
Now the eighteenth chapter.
Description of the lineage of Svāyambhuva.

18.s:
agnir uvāca
priyavratottānapādau manoḥ svāyambhuvāt sutau /
ajījanatsa tāṃ kanyāṃ śatarūpāṃ taponvitām(3) //
:n
1 bhūtamuccāvacaṃ hy ajāditi kha, gha, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
sāndhyāṃstair ayajan devān bhūtamuccāvacaṃ prajā iti ṅa,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 niścitamiti kha,cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 ajījanat sutāṃ kanyāṃ sadrūpāñca taponvitāmiti ga,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / ajījanat sutāṃ kanyāṃ śatarūpāṃ
taponvitāmiti ṅa,cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 42
18.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
प्रियव्रतोत्तानपादौ मनोः स्वायम्भुवात् सुतौ /
अजीजनत्स तां कन्यां शतरूपां तपोन्विताम्(3) //
:न्
1 भूतमुच्चावचं ह्य् अजादिति ख, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
सान्ध्यांस्तैर् अयजन् देवान् भूतमुच्चावचं प्रजा इति ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 निश्चितमिति ख,चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 अजीजनत् सुतां कन्यां सद्रूपाञ्च तपोन्वितामिति ग,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / अजीजनत् सुतां कन्यां शतरूपां
तपोन्वितामिति ङ,चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 42
18.m:
Agni said:
Priyavrata and Uttānapāda were the two sons of Svāyambhuva Manu;
he begot that maiden Śatarūpā, endowed with ascetic austerity.
:n
1 "bhūtamuccāvacaṃ hy ajāt" is the reading of the two manuscripts marked kha and gha; "sāndhyāṃstair ayajan devān bhūtamuccāvacaṃ prajāḥ" is the reading of the manuscript marked ṅa.
2 "niścitam" is the reading of the manuscript marked kha.
3 "ajījanat sutāṃ kanyāṃ sadrūpāñca taponvitām" is the reading of the manuscript marked ga; "ajījanat sutāṃ kanyāṃ śatarūpāṃ taponvitām" is the reading of the manuscript marked ṅa.
:p 42

18.s:
kāmyāṃ(1) kardamabhāryātaḥ samrāṭ kukṣirvirāṭ prabhuḥ /
surucyāmuttamo jajñe putra uttānapādataḥ //
18.d:
काम्यां(1) कर्दमभार्यातः सम्राट् कुक्षिर्विराट् प्रभुः /
सुरुच्यामुत्तमो जज्ञे पुत्र उत्तानपादतः //
18.m:
From Kāmyā, the wife of Kardama, [were born] Samrāṭ, Kukṣi, and the lord Virāṭ.
In Suruci, a son, Uttama, was born from Uttānapāda;

18.s:
sunītyāntu dhruvaḥ putrastapastepe sa kīrtaye /
dhruvo varṣasahasrāṇi trīṇi divyāni he mune //
18.d:
सुनीत्यान्तु ध्रुवः पुत्रस्तपस्तेपे स कीर्तये /
ध्रुवो वर्षसहस्राणि त्रीणि दिव्यानि हे मुने //
18.m:
and in Sunīti, a son, Dhruva. He performed ascetic austerity for renown;
Dhruva [did so] for three thousand divine years, O sage.

18.s:
tasmai prīto hariḥ prādānmunyagre sthānakaṃ sthiram(2) /
ślokaṃ papāṭha hy uśanā vṛddhiṃ dṛṣṭvā sa tasya ca //
18.d:
तस्मै प्रीतो हरिः प्रादान्मुन्यग्रे स्थानकं स्थिरम्(2) /
श्लोकं पपाठ ह्य् उशना वृद्धिं दृष्ट्वा स तस्य च //
18.m:
Pleased with him, Hari granted a permanent station in front of the sages;
and seeing his advancement, Uśanas recited a verse:

18.s:
aho 'sya tapaso vīryamaho śrutamahodbhutam /
yamadya(3) purataḥ kṛtvā dhruvaṃ saptarṣayaḥ sthitāḥ //
18.d:
अहो ऽस्य तपसो वीर्यमहो श्रुतमहोद्भुतम् /
यमद्य(3) पुरतः कृत्वा ध्रुवं सप्तर्षयः स्थिताः //
18.m:
‘Ah, the power of his ascetic austerity! Ah, his sacred learning, most wonderful,
keeping which Dhruva in front of them the Seven Sages today stand!’

18.s:
tasmāt śiṣṭiñca(4) bhavyañca dhruvācchambhurvyajāyata /
śiṣṭerādhatta(5) suchāyā pañca putrānakalmaṣān //
18.d:
तस्मात् शिष्टिञ्च(4) भव्यञ्च ध्रुवाच्छम्भुर्व्यजायत /
शिष्टेराधत्त(5) सुछाया पञ्च पुत्रानकल्मषान् //
18.m:
From him, from Dhruva, Śiṣṭi and Bhavya were born; and Śambhu.
Suchāyā bore to Śiṣṭi five stainless sons:

18.s:
ripuṃ ripuñjayaṃ ripraṃ vṛkalaṃ vṛkatejasam /
riporādhatta bṛhatī cākṣuṣaṃ sarvatejasam //
18.d:
रिपुं रिपुञ्जयं रिप्रं वृकलं वृकतेजसम् /
रिपोराधत्त बृहती चाक्षुषं सर्वतेजसम् //
18.m:
Ripu, Ripuñjaya, Ripra, Vṛkala, and Vṛkatejas.
To Ripu, Bṛhatī bore Cākṣuṣa, possessed of all splendor.

18.s:
ajījanat puṣkariṇyāṃ vīriṇyāṃ cākṣuṣo manum /
manorajāyanta daśa naḍvalāyāṃ sutottamāḥ //
18.d:
अजीजनत् पुष्करिण्यां वीरिण्यां चाक्षुषो मनुम् /
मनोरजायन्त दश नड्वलायां सुतोत्तमाः //
18.m:
Cākṣuṣa begot Manu upon Puṣkariṇī, the daughter of Vīraṇa;
to Manu ten excellent sons were born of Naḍvalā:

18.s:
ūruḥ(6) puruḥ śatadyumnastapasvī satyavākkaviḥ /
agniṣṭuratirātraś ca sudyumnaścābhimanyukaḥ //
18.d:
ऊरुः(6) पुरुः शतद्युम्नस्तपस्वी सत्यवाक्कविः /
अग्निष्टुरतिरात्रश् च सुद्युम्नश्चाभिमन्युकः //
18.m:
Ūru, Puru, Śatadyumna, the ascetic Satyavāc, Kavi,
Agniṣṭut, Atirātra, Sudyumna, and Abhimanyu.

18.s:
ūrorajanayat putrān ṣaḍagneyī mahāprabhān /
aṅgaṃ sumanasaṃ svātiṃ kratumaṅgirasaṅgayam //
18.d:
ऊरोरजनयत् पुत्रान् षडग्नेयी महाप्रभान् /
अङ्गं सुमनसं स्वातिं क्रतुमङ्गिरसङ्गयम् //
18.m:
Āgneyī bore to Ūru six sons of great radiance:
Aṅga, Sumanas, Svāti, Kratu, Aṅgiras, and Gaya.

18.s:
aṅgāt sunīthāpatyaṃ vai veṇamekaṃ vyajāyata /
:n
1 kāmyā iti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
2 sthānamuttamamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 yadatra iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 tasmāt śliṣṭiñca iti ga, gha, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
5 śliṣṭeārādhatta iti kha, gha, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
6 urūriti kha,ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
:p 43
arakṣakaḥ pāparataḥ sa hato munibhiḥ kuśaiḥ //
18.d:
अङ्गात् सुनीथापत्यं वै वेणमेकं व्यजायत /
:न्
1 काम्या इति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
2 स्थानमुत्तममिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 यदत्र इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 तस्मात् श्लिष्टिञ्च इति ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
5 श्लिष्टेआराधत्त इति ख, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
6 उरूरिति ख,ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
:प् 43
अरक्षकः पापरतः स हतो मुनिभिः कुशैः //
18.m:
From Aṅga, one child indeed, Veṇa, was born to Sunīthā;
:n
1 "kāmyāḥ" is the reading of the two manuscripts marked ga and ṅa.
2 "sthānamuttamam" is the reading of the manuscript marked ṅa.
3 "yadatra" is the reading of the manuscript marked ṅa.
4 "tasmāt śliṣṭiñca" is the reading of the two manuscripts marked ga and gha.
5 "śliṣṭerādhatta" is the reading of the two manuscripts marked kha and gha.
6 "uruḥ" is the reading of the three manuscripts marked kha, ga, and ṅa.
:p 43
providing no protection, devoted to sin, he was slain by the sages with kuśa grass.

18.s:
prajārthamṛṣayothāsya mamanthurdakṣiṇaṃ karaṃ /
veṇasya mathito pāṇau sambabhūva pṛthur nṛpaḥ //
18.d:
प्रजार्थमृषयोथास्य ममन्थुर्दक्षिणं करं /
वेणस्य मथितो पाणौ सम्बभूव पृथुर् नृपः //
18.m:
Then, for the sake of offspring, the sages churned his right hand;
from the churned hand of Veṇa, King Pṛthu was born.

18.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā munayaḥ prāhureṣa vai muditāḥ prajāḥ /
kariṣyati mahātejā yaśaś ca prāpsyate mahat //
18.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा मुनयः प्राहुरेष वै मुदिताः प्रजाः /
करिष्यति महातेजा यशश् च प्राप्स्यते महत् //
18.m: Seeing him, the sages said: "He indeed will gladden the subjects; / endowed with great majesty, he will attain great fame."

18.s:
sa dhanvī kavacī jātastejasā nirdahanniva /
pṛthurvaiṇyaḥ prajāḥ sarvā rarakṣa kṣetrapūrvajaḥ //
18.d:
स धन्वी कवची जातस्तेजसा निर्दहन्निव /
पृथुर्वैण्यः प्रजाः सर्वा ररक्ष क्षेत्रपूर्वजः //
18.m: Born with a bow and clad in armour, burning as if with fiery energy, / Pṛthu, the son of Vena, the first ruler of the realm, protected all subjects.

18.s:
rājasūyābhiṣiktānāmādyaḥ(1) sa pṛthivīpatiḥ /
tasmāccaiva samutpannau nipuṇau sūtamāgadhau //
18.d:
राजसूयाभिषिक्तानामाद्यः(1) स पृथिवीपतिः /
तस्माच्चैव समुत्पन्नौ निपुणौ सूतमागधौ //
18.m: He was the first of the earth's kings consecrated in the Rājasūya sacrifice; / and from him were born the skilled bard (sūta) and herald (māgadha).

18.s:
tatstotrañcakraturvīrau rājābhūjjanarañjanāt /
dugdhā gaustena śasyārthaṃ prajānāṃ jīvanāya ca //
18.d:
तत्स्तोत्रञ्चक्रतुर्वीरौ राजाभूज्जनरञ्जनात् /
दुग्धा गौस्तेन शस्यार्थं प्रजानां जीवनाय च //
18.m: The two heroic singers composed his praise; he became king by gladdening the people. / By him the cow [of the earth] was milked for crops and for the livelihood of the subjects,

18.s:
saha devair munigaṇair gandharvaiḥ sāpsarogaṇaiḥ /
pitṛbhirdānavaiḥ sarpair vīrudbhiḥ parvatair janaiḥ //
18.d:
सह देवैर् मुनिगणैर् गन्धर्वैः साप्सरोगणैः /
पितृभिर्दानवैः सर्पैर् वीरुद्भिः पर्वतैर् जनैः //
18.m: along with the gods, the hosts of sages, the gandharvas together with the hosts of apsarases, / the ancestors, the dānavas, the serpents, the plants, the mountains, and people.

18.s:
teṣu teṣu ca pātreṣu duhyamānā vasundharā /
prādādyathepsitaṃ kṣīrantena prāṇānadhārayat //
18.d:
तेषु तेषु च पात्रेषु दुह्यमाना वसुन्धरा /
प्रादाद्यथेप्सितं क्षीरन्तेन प्राणानधारयत् //
18.m: Milked into various respective vessels, the earth / yielded the milk that was desired, and with that he sustained life.

18.s:
pṛthoḥ putrau tu dharmajñau jajñāte 'ntardvipālinau /
śikhaṇḍī havirdhānamantardhānāt vyajāyata //
18.d:
पृथोः पुत्रौ तु धर्मज्ञौ जज्ञाते ऽन्तर्द्विपालिनौ /
शिखण्डी हविर्धानमन्तर्धानात् व्यजायत //
18.m: To Pṛthu were born two sons who knew righteousness, Antardhi and Pālin. / From Antardhāna was born Havirdhāna through Śikhaṇḍī.

18.s:
havirdhānāt ṣaḍāgneyī dhīṣaṇājanayat sutān /
prācīnavarhiṣaṃ śukraṃ(2) gayaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ vrajājinau //
18.d:
हविर्धानात् षडाग्नेयी धीषणाजनयत् सुतान् /
प्राचीनवर्हिषं शुक्रं(2) गयं कृष्णं व्रजाजिनौ //
18.m: Dhīṣaṇā, daughter of Agni, bore to Havirdhāna six sons: / Prācīnabarhis, Śukra, Gaya, Kṛṣṇa, Vraja, and Ajina.

18.s:
prācīnāgrāḥ kuśāstasya pṛthivyāṃ yajato yataḥ /
prācīnavarhirbhagavān mahānāsītprajāpatiḥ //
18.d:
प्राचीनाग्राः कुशास्तस्य पृथिव्यां यजतो यतः /
प्राचीनवर्हिर्भगवान् महानासीत्प्रजापतिः //
18.m: Because his sacrificial grass had eastward points when he sacrificed upon the earth, / the venerable Prācīnabarhis became a great lord of creatures.

18.s:
savarṇādhatta(3) sāmudrī daśa prācīnavarhiṣaḥ /
:n
1 rājasūyābhivyaktānāmādya iti kha,cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 śubhramiti ga,cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 suvarṇādhatta iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 44
sarve pracetaso nāma dhanurvedasya pāragāḥ //
18.d:
सवर्णाधत्त(3) सामुद्री दश प्राचीनवर्हिषः /
:न्
1 राजसूयाभिव्यक्तानामाद्य इति ख,चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 शुभ्रमिति ग,चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 सुवर्णाधत्त इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 44
सर्वे प्रचेतसो नाम धनुर्वेदस्य पारगाः //
18.m:
Savarṇā, daughter of the ocean, bore ten sons to Prācīnabarhis,
[Note]
1 The reading in the manuscript marked kha is: "rājasūyābhivyaktānāmādya".
2 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is: "śubhram".
3 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is: "suvarṇādhatta". / Page 44
all named the Pracetases, who had mastered the science of archery.

18.s:
apṛthagdharmacaraṇās te tapyanta mahattapaḥ /
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi samudrasalileśayāḥ //
18.d:
अपृथग्धर्मचरणास् ते तप्यन्त महत्तपः /
दशवर्षसहस्राणि समुद्रसलिलेशयाः //
18.m: Practising a common duty, they performed great ascetic austerity, / lying in the waters of the ocean for ten thousand years.

18.s:
prajāpatitvaṃ samprāpya tuṣṭā viṣṇoś ca nirgatāḥ /
bhūḥ khaṃ vyāptaṃ hi tarubhistāṃstarūnadahaṃś ca te //
18.d:
प्रजापतित्वं सम्प्राप्य तुष्टा विष्णोश् च निर्गताः /
भूः खं व्याप्तं हि तरुभिस्तांस्तरूनदहंश् च ते //
18.m: Having attained the status of lords of creatures, pleased with Viṣṇu, they emerged. / Earth and sky were covered with trees, and they burned down those trees

18.s:
mukhajāgnimarudbhyāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā cātha drumakṣayam /
upagamyābravīdetān rājā somaḥ prajāpatīn //
18.d:
मुखजाग्निमरुद्भ्यां च दृष्ट्वा चाथ द्रुमक्षयम् /
उपगम्याब्रवीदेतान् राजा सोमः प्रजापतीन् //
18.m: with fire and wind born from their mouths. Then, seeing the destruction of the trees, / King Soma approached and spoke to these lords of creatures:

18.s:
kopaṃ yacchata dāsyanti kanyāṃ vo māriṣāṃ varām /
tapasvino muneḥ kaṇḍoḥ(2) pramlocāyāṃ mamaiva ca //
18.d:
कोपं यच्छत दास्यन्ति कन्यां वो मारिषां वराम् /
तपस्विनो मुनेः कण्डोः(2) प्रम्लोचायां ममैव च //
18.m: "Restrain your anger! They will give you the excellent maiden Māriṣā, / [begotten] of the ascetic sage Kaṇḍu upon Pramlocā, and [nourished] by me.

18.s:
bhaviṣyaṃ jānatā sṛṣṭā bhāryā vo 'stu kulaṅkarī /
asyāmutpatsyate dakṣaḥ prajāḥ saṃvardhayiṣyati //
18.d:
भविष्यं जानता सृष्टा भार्या वो ऽस्तु कुलङ्करी /
अस्यामुत्पत्स्यते दक्षः प्रजाः संवर्धयिष्यति //
18.m: Created by one who knew what was to come, let her be your lineage-founding wife; / in her, Dakṣa will be born and will multiply the subjects."

18.s:
pracetasastāṃ jagṛhurdakṣosyāñca tato 'bhavat /
acarāṃś ca carāṃś caiva dvipadotha catuṣpadaḥ //
18.d:
प्रचेतसस्तां जगृहुर्दक्षोस्याञ्च ततो ऽभवत् /
अचरांश् च चरांश् चैव द्विपदोथ चतुष्पदः //
18.m: The Pracetases took her, and from her Dakṣa was born. / Having created by his mind immobile and mobile beings, two-footed and four-footed creatures,

18.s:
sa sṛṣṭvā manasā(2) dakṣaḥ paścādasṛjata striyaḥ /
dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa //
18.d:
स सृष्ट्वा मनसा(2) दक्षः पश्चादसृजत स्त्रियः /
ददौ स दश धर्माय कश्यपाय त्रयोदश //
18.m: Dakṣa afterwards created women. / He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa,

18.s:
saptāviṃśati somāya catastro 'riṣṭanemine /
dve caiva bahuputrāya dve caivāṅgirase adāt(3) //
18.d:
सप्ताविंशति सोमाय चतस्त्रो ऽरिष्टनेमिने /
द्वे चैव बहुपुत्राय द्वे चैवाङ्गिरसे अदात्(3) //
18.m: twenty-seven to Soma, four to Ariṣṭanemi, / two to Bahuputra, and two to Aṅgiras.

18.s:
tāsu devāś ca nāgādyā maithunānmanasā purā /
dharmasargampravakṣyāmi daśapatnīṣu dharmataḥ //
18.d:
तासु देवाश् च नागाद्या मैथुनान्मनसा पुरा /
धर्मसर्गम्प्रवक्ष्यामि दशपत्नीषु धर्मतः //
18.m: Through union in them, the gods, snakes, and others were born, who earlier had been born from the mind. / I shall declare the creation of Dharma through his ten wives in proper order:

18.s:
viśvedevāstu viśvāyāḥ sādhyān sādhyā vyajāyata /
maruttvayā maruttvanto vasostu vasavo 'bhavan //
18.d:
विश्वेदेवास्तु विश्वायाः साध्यान् साध्या व्यजायत /
मरुत्त्वया मरुत्त्वन्तो वसोस्तु वसवो ऽभवन् //
18.m: From Viśvā were born the Viśvedevas; Sādhyā gave birth to the Sādhyas; / by Marutvatī were the Marutvats; and the Vasus were born from Vasu.

18.s:
bhānostu bhānavaḥ putrā muhūrtāstu muhūrtajāḥ /
:n
1 kaṇṭhoriti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ karṇoriti
ṅa,cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 sa dṛṣṭvā manasā iti kha, ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 dve caiva bhāṇḍave tata iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 45
sambāyā(1) dharmato ghoṣo nāgavīthī(2) ca yāmijā //
18.d:
भानोस्तु भानवः पुत्रा मुहूर्तास्तु मुहूर्तजाः /
:न्
1 कण्ठोरिति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः कर्णोरिति
ङ,चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 स दृष्ट्वा मनसा इति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 द्वे चैव भाण्डवे तत इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 45
सम्बाया(1) धर्मतो घोषो नागवीथी(2) च यामिजा //
18.m:
The Bhānus were the sons of Bhānu; the Muhūrtajas were born of Muhūrtā;
[Note]
1 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is "kaṇṭhoriti"; the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is "karṇoriti".
2 The reading in the manuscripts marked kha and ga is: "sa dṛṣṭvā manasā".
3 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is: "dve caiva bhāṇḍave tataḥ". / Page 45
Ghoṣa was born from Lambā by Dharma; and Nāgavīthī was born of Yāmi.

18.s:
pṛthivīviṣayaṃ sarvamarundhatyāṃ vyajāyata /
saṅkalpāyāstu saṅkalpā indor nakṣatrataḥ sutāḥ //
18.d:
पृथिवीविषयं सर्वमरुन्धत्यां व्यजायत /
सङ्कल्पायास्तु सङ्कल्पा इन्दोर् नक्षत्रतः सुताः //
18.m: Everything pertaining to the earth was born in Arundhatī; / the Saṅkalpas were born from Saṅkalpā; and the sons of Indu were born of the Nakṣatras.

18.s:
āpo dhruvañca somañca dharaś caivānilonalaḥ(3) /
pratyūṣaś ca prabhāvaś ca vasavoṣṭau ca nāmataḥ //
18.d:
आपो ध्रुवञ्च सोमञ्च धरश् चैवानिलोनलः(3) /
प्रत्यूषश् च प्रभावश् च वसवोष्टौ च नामतः //
18.m: Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala, / Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa—these are the eight Vasus by name.

18.s:
āpasya putro vaitaṇḍyaḥ śramaḥ śānto munis tathā /
dhruvasya kālo lokānto varcāḥ somasya vai sutaḥ //
18.d:
आपस्य पुत्रो वैतण्ड्यः श्रमः शान्तो मुनिस् तथा /
ध्रुवस्य कालो लोकान्तो वर्चाः सोमस्य वै सुतः //
18.m: The sons of Āpa were Vaitaṇḍya, Śrama, Śānta, and the sage [Muni]; / the son of Dhruva was Kāla, the end of the worlds; Varcas was the son of Soma.

18.s:
dharasya putro draviṇo(4) hutahavyavahas tathā /
manoharāyāḥ śiśiraḥ prāṇotha ramaṇas tathā(5) //
18.d:
धरस्य पुत्रो द्रविणो(4) हुतहव्यवहस् तथा /
मनोहरायाः शिशिरः प्राणोथ रमणस् तथा(5) //
18.m: The son of Dhara was Draviṇa and Hutahavyavaha; / from Manoharā were Śiśira, Prāṇa, and Ramaṇa.

18.s:
purojavonilasyāsīdavijñāto 'nalasya ca /
agniputraḥ kumāraś ca śarastambe vyajāyata //
18.d:
पुरोजवोनिलस्यासीदविज्ञातो ऽनलस्य च /
अग्निपुत्रः कुमारश् च शरस्तम्बे व्यजायत //
18.m: Purojava was the son of Anila; Avijñāta was the son of Anala. / Kumāra, the son of Agni, was born in a clump of reeds;

18.s:
tasya śākho viśākhaś ca naigameyaś ca pṛṣṭajaḥ /
kṛttikātaḥ kārttikeyo yatiḥ sanatkumārakaḥ(6) //
18.d:
तस्य शाखो विशाखश् च नैगमेयश् च पृष्टजः /
कृत्तिकातः कार्त्तिकेयो यतिः सनत्कुमारकः(6) //
18.m: his [brothers/forms] were Śākha, Viśākha, and Naigameya, born from his back. / From the Kṛttikās came Kārttikeya, the ascetic Sanatkumāra.

18.s:
pratyūṣāddevalo jajñe viśvakarmā prabhāvataḥ /
kartā śilpasahasrāṇāṃ tridaśānāñca vardhakiḥ //
18.d:
प्रत्यूषाद्देवलो जज्ञे विश्वकर्मा प्रभावतः /
कर्ता शिल्पसहस्राणां त्रिदशानाञ्च वर्धकिः //
18.m: From Pratyūṣa was born Devala; Viśvakarman was born from Prabhāsa, / the creator of thousands of arts and crafts, and the architect of the gods;

18.s:
manuṣyāścopjīvanti śilpaṃ vai bhūṣaṇādikaṃ /
surabhī(7) kaśyapādrudrānekādaśa vijajñuṣī //
18.d:
मनुष्याश्चोप्जीवन्ति शिल्पं वै भूषणादिकं /
सुरभी(7) कश्यपाद्रुद्रानेकादश विजज्ञुषी //
18.m: and human beings sustain themselves by his craftsmanship in ornaments and the like. / Surabhi bore the eleven Rudras to Kaśyapa,

18.s:
mahādevaprasādena tapasā bhāvitā satī /
:n
1 lambāyā iti ga,cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 nagavīthī iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 dharmaś caivānilonala iti kha, ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 dhariṣa iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 maraṇastatheti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
6 jātaḥ sanatkumārata iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
7 yuvatī iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 46
ajaikapādahirbraghnastvaṣṭā rudrāś ca sattama(1) //
18.d:
महादेवप्रसादेन तपसा भाविता सती /
:न्
1 लम्बाया इति ग,चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 नगवीथी इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 धर्मश् चैवानिलोनल इति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 धरिष इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 मरणस्तथेति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
6 जातः सनत्कुमारत इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
7 युवती इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 46
अजैकपादहिर्ब्रघ्नस्त्वष्टा रुद्राश् च सत्तम(1) //
18.m:
the virtuous one having been inspired through ascetic austerity by the grace of Mahādeva:
[Note]
1 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is: "lambāyāḥ".
2 The reading in the manuscript marked kha is: "nagavīthī".
3 The reading in the manuscripts marked kha and ga is: "dharmaś caivānilonalaḥ".
4 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is: "dhariṣaḥ".
5 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is: "maraṇastathā".
6 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is: "jātaḥ sanatkumārataḥ".
7 The reading in the manuscript marked ga is: "yuvatī". / Page 46
Ajaikapād, Ahirbudhnya, Tvaṣṭṛ, and the Rudras, O best of men;

18.s:
tvaṣṭuś caivātmajaḥ śrīmānviśvarūpo mahāyaśāḥ /
haraś ca bahurūpaś ca tryambakaścāparājitaḥ //
18.d:
त्वष्टुश् चैवात्मजः श्रीमान्विश्वरूपो महायशाः /
हरश् च बहुरूपश् च त्र्यम्बकश्चापराजितः //
18.m: and the son of Tvaṣṭṛ was the glorious and far-famed Viśvarūpa; / Hara, Bahurūpa, Tryambaka, Aparājita,

18.s:
vṛṣākapiś ca śambhuś ca kapardī raivatas tathā /
mṛgavyādhasya sarpaś ca kapālī daśa caikakaḥ /
rudrāṇāṃ ca śataṃ lakṣaṃ yair vyāptaṃ sacarācaraṃ //
:e ity ādimāhāpurāṇe āgneye jagatsargavarṇanaṃ nāma
aṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athonaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
kaśyapavaṃśavarṇanam
18.d:
वृषाकपिश् च शम्भुश् च कपर्दी रैवतस् तथा /
मृगव्याधस्य सर्पश् च कपाली दश चैककः /
रुद्राणां च शतं लक्षं यैर् व्याप्तं सचराचरं //
:ए इत्य् आदिमाहापुराणे आग्नेये जगत्सर्गवर्णनं नाम
अष्टादशो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथोनविंशतितमो ऽध्यायः
कश्यपवंशवर्णनम्
18.m:
Vṛṣākapi, Śambhu, Kapardin, Raivata, / Mṛgavyādha, Sarpa, and Kapālin—these are the eleven Rudras; / and there are a hundred and a hundred thousand Rudras by whom all moving and unmoving things are pervaded.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, named "The Description of the Creation of the Universe", in the Agni Mahāpurāṇa.
Now the nineteenth chapter:
Description of the Lineage of Kaśyapa

19.s:
agnir uvāca
kaśyapasya vede sargamadityādiṣu he mune /
cākṣuṣe tuṣitā devāste 'dityāṃ kaśyapātpunaḥ //
19.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
कश्यपस्य वेदे सर्गमदित्यादिषु हे मुने /
चाक्षुषे तुषिता देवास्ते ऽदित्यां कश्यपात्पुनः //
19.m: Agni said: / Hear of the creation of Kaśyapa through Aditi and the others, O sage. / The gods who were the Tuṣitas in the Cākṣuṣa [manvantara] were again born to Kaśyapa in Aditi:

19.s:
āsan viṣṇuś ca śakraś ca tvaṣṭā dhātā tathāryamā /
pūṣā vivasvān savitā mitrotha varuṇo bhagaḥ //
19.d:
आसन् विष्णुश् च शक्रश् च त्वष्टा धाता तथार्यमा /
पूषा विवस्वान् सविता मित्रोथ वरुणो भगः //
19.m: They were Viṣṇu, Śakra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Dhātṛ, and Aryaman, / Pūṣan, Vivasvan, Savitṛ, Mitra, Varuṇa, Bhaga,

19.s:
aṃśuś ca dvādaśādityā āsan vaivasvatentare /
ariṣṭanemipatrīnāmapatyānīha ṣoḍaśa //
19.d:
अंशुश् च द्वादशादित्या आसन् वैवस्वतेन्तरे /
अरिष्टनेमिपत्रीनामपत्यानीह षोडश //
19.m: and Aṃśa—these were the twelve Ādityas in the Vaivasvata interval. / The offspring of the wives of Ariṣṭanemi here were sixteen;

19.s:
bahuputrastha viduṣaś catasro vidyutaḥ sutāḥ(2) /
pratyaṅgirajāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ kṛśāśvasya surāyudhāḥ //
19.d:
बहुपुत्रस्थ विदुषश् चतस्रो विद्युतः सुताः(2) /
प्रत्यङ्गिरजाः श्रेष्ठाः कृशाश्वस्य सुरायुधाः //
19.m: the four lightning-daughters were of the wise Bahuputra; / the divine weapons of Kṛśāśva were born from Pratyaṅgiras, the most excellent ones.

19.s:
udayāstamane sūrye tadvadete yuge yuge /
hiraṇyakaśipurdityāṃ hiraṇyākṣaś ca kaśyapāt //
:n
1 saptama iti kha ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 smṛtā iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 47
19.d:
उदयास्तमने सूर्ये तद्वदेते युगे युगे /
हिरण्यकशिपुर्दित्यां हिरण्याक्षश् च कश्यपात् //
:न्
1 सप्तम इति ख ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 स्मृता इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 47
19.m:
They appear in every yuga at sunrise and sunset in the same way. / Hiraṇyakaśipu and Hiraṇyākṣa were born to Kaśyapa from Diti.
[Footnote]
1. "saptamaḥ" is the reading in the manuscripts marked kha and ṅa.
2. "smṛtāḥ" is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.

19.s:
siṃhikā cābhavat kanyā vipracitteḥ parigrahaḥ /
rāhuprabhṛtayastasyāṃ saiṃhikeyā iti śrutāḥ //
19.d:
सिंहिका चाभवत् कन्या विप्रचित्तेः परिग्रहः /
राहुप्रभृतयस्तस्यां सैंहिकेया इति श्रुताः //
19.m: And Siṃhikā was a daughter who became the wife of Vipracitti; / from her were born Rāhu and others, celebrated as the Saiṃhikeyas.

19.s:
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putrāś catvāraḥ prathitaujasaḥ /
anuhrādaś ca hrādaś ca prahrādaścātivaiṣṇavaḥ //
19.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोः पुत्राश् चत्वारः प्रथितौजसः /
अनुह्रादश् च ह्रादश् च प्रह्रादश्चातिवैष्णवः //
19.m: Hiraṇyakaśipu had four sons of renowned might: / Anuhrāda, Hrāda, and Prahrāda, devoted to Viṣṇu,

19.s:
saṃhrādaś ca caturthobhūt hrādaputro hradas tathā /
hradasya putra āyuṣmān(1) śibirvāskala eva ca //
19.d:
संह्रादश् च चतुर्थोभूत् ह्रादपुत्रो ह्रदस् तथा /
ह्रदस्य पुत्र आयुष्मान्(1) शिबिर्वास्कल एव च //
19.m: and Saṃhrāda was the fourth. Hrāda's son was Hrada, / and Hrada's long-lived son was Śibi, as well as Vāskala.

19.s:
virovanastu prāhrādirbalirjajñe virocanāt /
baleḥ putraśataṃ tvāsīdvāṇaśreṣṭhaṃ(2) mahāmune //
19.d:
विरोवनस्तु प्राह्रादिर्बलिर्जज्ञे विरोचनात् /
बलेः पुत्रशतं त्वासीद्वाणश्रेष्ठं(2) महामुने //
19.m: Virocana was the son of Prahrāda; from Virocana, Bali was born. / Bali had a hundred sons, of whom Bāṇa was the eldest, O great sage.

19.s:
purākalpe hi bāṇena prasādyomāpatiṃ varaḥ(3) /
pārśvato vihariṣyāmītyevam prāptaś ca īśvarāt(4) //
19.d:
पुराकल्पे हि बाणेन प्रसाद्योमापतिं वरः(3) /
पार्श्वतो विहरिष्यामीत्येवम् प्राप्तश् च ईश्वरात्(4) //
19.m: For in a previous cosmic cycle, Bāṇa, having propitiated the husband of Umā, obtained a boon / from the Lord: 'I shall sport at your side.'

19.s:
hiraṇyākṣasutāḥ pañca śambaraḥ śakunistviti(5) /
dvimūrdhā śaṅkurāryaś ca(6) śatamāsan danoḥ sutāḥ //
19.d:
हिरण्याक्षसुताः पञ्च शम्बरः शकुनिस्त्विति(5) /
द्विमूर्धा शङ्कुरार्यश् च(6) शतमासन् दनोः सुताः //
19.m: Hiraṇyākṣa had five sons: Śambara, Śakuni, / Dvimūrdhan, Śaṅku, and Ārya. Danu had a hundred sons.

19.s:
svarbhānostu prabhā kanyā pulomnastu śacī smṛtā /
upadānavī hayaśirā śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī //
19.d:
स्वर्भानोस्तु प्रभा कन्या पुलोम्नस्तु शची स्मृता /
उपदानवी हयशिरा शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी //
19.m: Svarbhānu's daughter was Prabhā, and Puloman's is known as Śacī; / Upadānavī, Hayaśiras, and Śarmiṣṭhā the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan.

19.s:
pulomā kālakā caiva vaiśvānarasute ubhe /
kaśyapasya tu bhārye dve tayoḥ putrāś ca koṭayaḥ //
19.d:
पुलोमा कालका चैव वैश्वानरसुते उभे /
कश्यपस्य तु भार्ये द्वे तयोः पुत्राश् च कोटयः //
19.m: Pulomā and Kālakā were both daughters of Vaiśvānara; / they were two wives of Kaśyapa, and their sons numbered in the tens of millions.

19.s:
prahrādasya catuṣkoṭyo nivātakavacāḥ kule /
tāmrāyāḥ ṣaṭ sutāḥ syuś ca kākī śvenī ca bhāsyapi //
19.d:
प्रह्रादस्य चतुष्कोट्यो निवातकवचाः कुले /
ताम्रायाः षट् सुताः स्युश् च काकी श्वेनी च भास्यपि //
19.m: In the lineage of Prahrāda were forty million Nivātakavacas. / Tāmrā had six daughters: Kākī, Śvenī, and Bhāsī,

19.s:
gṛdhrikā śuci sugrīvā(7) tābhyaḥ kākādayo 'bhavan /
:n
1 saṃhrādaputra āyuṣmāniti kha, ga, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
2 vāṇajyeṣṭhamiti kha, ga, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
3 prabhumiti kha, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
4 ity evaṃ prāptamīśvarāditi kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 jharjharaḥ śakunistvatīti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / śaknistvatheti
ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
6 dvimūrdhā śambarādyāś ca iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
7 gṛdhrikā ca śucigrīvo iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
gṛdhrikāśucisugrīvo iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 48
aśvāścoṣṭrāś ca tāmrāyā aruṇo garuḍas tathā //
19.d:
गृध्रिका शुचि सुग्रीवा(7) ताभ्यः काकादयो ऽभवन् /
:न्
1 संह्रादपुत्र आयुष्मानिति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
2 वाणज्येष्ठमिति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
3 प्रभुमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
4 इत्य् एवं प्राप्तमीश्वरादिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 झर्झरः शकुनिस्त्वतीति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / शक्निस्त्वथेति
ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
6 द्विमूर्धा शम्बराद्याश् च इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
7 गृध्रिका च शुचिग्रीवो इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
गृध्रिकाशुचिसुग्रीवो इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 48
अश्वाश्चोष्ट्राश् च ताम्राया अरुणो गरुडस् तथा //
19.m:
Gṛdhrikā, Śuci, and Sugrīvā; from them crows and other birds were born.
[Footnote]
1. "saṃhrādaputra āyuṣmān" is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ga.
2. "vāṇajyeṣṭham" is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ga.
3. "prabhum" is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha.
4. "ity evaṃ prāptamīśvarāt" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
5. "jharjharaḥ śakunistvatī" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha; "śaknistvathe" is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
6. "dvimūrdhā śambarādyāś ca" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
7. "gṛdhrikā ca śucigrīvo" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha; "gṛdhrikāśucisugrīvo" is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
Horses and camels also came from Tāmrā, as well as Aruṇa and Garuḍa.

19.s:
vinatāyāḥ sahasrantu sarpāś ca surasābhavāḥ /
kādraveyāḥ sahasrantu śeṣavāsukitakṣakāḥ //
19.d:
विनतायाः सहस्रन्तु सर्पाश् च सुरसाभवाः /
काद्रवेयाः सहस्रन्तु शेषवासुकितक्षकाः //
19.m: Vinatā had a thousand [offspring], and serpents were born from Surasā; / Kadrū's progeny were a thousand, including Śeṣa, Vāsuki, and Takṣaka.

19.s:
daṃṣṭriṇaḥ krodhavaśajā dharotthāḥ(1) pakṣiṇo jale /
surabhyāṃ gomahiṣyādi irotpannāstṛṇādayaḥ //
19.d:
दंष्ट्रिणः क्रोधवशजा धरोत्थाः(1) पक्षिणो जले /
सुरभ्यां गोमहिष्यादि इरोत्पन्नास्तृणादयः //
19.m: Fanged beasts were born of Krodhavaśā; from Dharā arose the birds upon the water; / from Surabhi arose cows, buffaloes, and the like; and from Irā were born grasses and other plants.

19.s:
svasāyāṃ yakṣarakṣāṃsi muneraśvarasobhavan /
ariṣṭāyāntu gandharvāḥ kaśyapāddhi sthirañcaraṃ(2) //
19.d:
स्वसायां यक्षरक्षांसि मुनेरश्वरसोभवन् /
अरिष्टायान्तु गन्धर्वाः कश्यपाद्धि स्थिरञ्चरं(2) //
19.m: From Svasā were born the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas; from the sage [Kaśyapa] arose the horses and Apsarases; / from Ariṣṭā the Gandharvas; thus from Kaśyapa came the stationary and the moving [creation].

19.s:
eṣāṃ putrādayo 'saṅkhyā devair vai dānavā jitāḥ(3) /
ditirvinaṣṭaputrā vai toṣayāmāsa kaśyapaṃ //
19.d:
एषां पुत्रादयो ऽसङ्ख्या देवैर् वै दानवा जिताः(3) /
दितिर्विनष्टपुत्रा वै तोषयामास कश्यपं //
19.m: Their sons and descendants were innumerable; the Dānavas were defeated by the gods. / Diti, whose sons had perished, propitiated Kaśyapa.

19.s:
putramindraprahartāramicchatī prāpa kaśyapāt /
pādāprakṣālanāt suptā tasyā garbhaṃ jaghāna ha //
19.d:
पुत्रमिन्द्रप्रहर्तारमिच्छती प्राप कश्यपात् /
पादाप्रक्षालनात् सुप्ता तस्या गर्भं जघान ह //
19.m: Desiring a son who would strike down Indra, she obtained [one] from Kaśyapa. / When she fell asleep without washing her feet, he struck the embryo [in] her [womb].

19.s:
chidramanviṣya cendrastu te devā maruto 'bhavan /
śakrasyaikonapañcāśatsahāyā dīptatejasaḥ //
19.d:
छिद्रमन्विष्य चेन्द्रस्तु ते देवा मरुतो ऽभवन् /
शक्रस्यैकोनपञ्चाशत्सहाया दीप्ततेजसः //
19.m: Seeking an opening, Indra [did this]; they became the gods, the Maruts, / forty-nine companions of Śakra, radiant with splendour.

19.s:
etatsarvaṃ harirbrahmā abhiṣicya pṛthuṃ nṛpaṃ /
dadau krameṇa rājyāni anyeṣāmadhipo hariḥ //
19.d:
एतत्सर्वं हरिर्ब्रह्मा अभिषिच्य पृथुं नृपं /
ददौ क्रमेण राज्यानि अन्येषामधिपो हरिः //
19.m: Having consecrated King Pṛthu over all this, Hari, Brahmā, / and Hari the overlord bestowed kingdoms upon the others in turn:

19.s:
dvijauṣadhīnāṃ candraś ca apāntu varuṇo nṛpaḥ /
rājñāṃ vaiśravaṇo rājā sūryāṇāṃ viṣṇorīśvaraḥ //
19.d:
द्विजौषधीनां चन्द्रश् च अपान्तु वरुणो नृपः /
राज्ञां वैश्रवणो राजा सूर्याणां विष्णोरीश्वरः //
19.m: Candra was made king of the twice-born and medicinal herbs; Varuṇa of waters; / Vaiśravaṇa of kings; and Viṣṇu the lord of the solar deities.

19.s:
vasūnāṃ pāvako rājā marutāṃ vāsavaḥ prabhuḥ /
prajāpatīnāṃ dakṣo 'tha prahlādo dānavādhipaḥ //
19.d:
वसूनां पावको राजा मरुतां वासवः प्रभुः /
प्रजापतीनां दक्षो ऽथ प्रह्लादो दानवाधिपः //
19.m: Pāvaka was made king of the Vasus; Vāsava lord of the Maruts; / Dakṣa of the Prajāpatis; and Prahlāda sovereign of the Dānavas.

19.s:
pitṝṇāṃ ca yamo rājā bhūtādīnāṃ haraḥ(4) prabhuḥ /
himavāṃś caiva śailānāṃ nadīnāṃ sāgaraḥ prabhuḥ //
:n
1 dharaṇyā iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 kaśyapādi parasparamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 devair dāityāḥ parājitā iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 bhūtānāñca hara iti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 49
19.d:
पितॄणां च यमो राजा भूतादीनां हरः(4) प्रभुः /
हिमवांश् चैव शैलानां नदीनां सागरः प्रभुः //
:न्
1 धरण्या इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 कश्यपादि परस्परमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 देवैर् दाइत्याः पराजिता इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 भूतानाञ्च हर इति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 49
19.m:
Yama was made king of the ancestors; Hara lord of the spirits and other beings; / Himavat lord of the mountains; and the ocean lord of the rivers.
[Footnote]
1. "dharaṇyāḥ" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2. "kaśyapādi parasparam" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
3. "devair daityāḥ parājitāḥ" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
4. "bhūtānāñ ca haraḥ" is the reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and ṅa.

19.s:
gāndharvāṇāṃ citraratho nāgānāmatha vāsukiḥ /
sarpāṇāṃ takṣako rājā garuḍaḥ pakṣiṇāmatha //
19.d:
गान्धर्वाणां चित्ररथो नागानामथ वासुकिः /
सर्पाणां तक्षको राजा गरुडः पक्षिणामथ //
19.m: Citraratha was made king of the Gandharvas; Vāsuki of the Nāgas; / Takṣaka of the serpents; and Garuḍa of the birds.

19.s:
airāvato gajendrāṇāṃ govṛṣotha gavāmapi /
mṛgaṇāmatha śārdūlaḥ plakṣo vanaspatīśvaraḥ //
19.d:
ऐरावतो गजेन्द्राणां गोवृषोथ गवामपि /
मृगणामथ शार्दूलः प्लक्षो वनस्पतीश्वरः //
19.m: Airāvata of noble elephants; the bull of cattle; / the tiger of beasts of prey; and the plakṣa tree the lord of trees.

19.s:
uccaiḥśravās tathāśvānāṃ sudhanvā pūrvapālakaḥ /
dakṣiṇasyāṃ śaṅkhapadaḥ ketumān pālako jale /
hiraṇyaromakaḥ saumye pratisargoyamīritaḥ //
:e ity ādimāhāpurāṇe āgneye pratisargavarṇanaṃ nāma
ūnaviṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha viṃśatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sargaviṣayakavarṇanaṃ
19.d:
उच्चैःश्रवास् तथाश्वानां सुधन्वा पूर्वपालकः /
दक्षिणस्यां शङ्खपदः केतुमान् पालको जले /
हिरण्यरोमकः सौम्ये प्रतिसर्गोयमीरितः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमाहापुराणे आग्नेये प्रतिसर्गवर्णनं नाम
ऊनविंशतितमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ विंशतितमो ऽध्यायः
सर्गविषयकवर्णनं
19.m:
Uccaiḥśravas of horses; Sudhanvan protector of the east; / Śaṅkhapada in the south; Ketumat protector in the water [of the west]; / and Hiraṇyaromaka in the north. Thus secondary creation has been declared.
Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, entitled "The Description of Secondary Creation," in the great and ancient Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the twentieth chapter.
The description regarding primary creation.

20.s:
agnir uvāca
prathamo mahataḥ sargo vijñeyo brahmaṇastu saḥ /
tanmātrāṇāṃ dvitīyastu bhūtasargo hi sa smṛtaḥ //
20.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
प्रथमो महतः सर्गो विज्ञेयो ब्रह्मणस्तु सः /
तन्मात्राणां द्वितीयस्तु भूतसर्गो हि स स्मृतः //
20.m: Agni said: / The first creation should be known as that of Mahat, which belongs to Brahmā. / The second is that of the subtle elements, known as the elemental creation.

20.s:
vaikārikastṛtīyastu sarga aindriyakaḥ smṛtaḥ /
ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargaḥ sambhūto buddhipūrvakaḥ //
20.d:
वैकारिकस्तृतीयस्तु सर्ग ऐन्द्रियकः स्मृतः /
इत्येष प्राकृतः सर्गः सम्भूतो बुद्धिपूर्वकः //
20.m: The third creation, originating from modification, is known as that of the sense organs. / Thus this is the primary creation, which arose preceded by intelligence.

20.s:
mukhyaḥ sargaś caturthastu mukhyā vai sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ /
tiryaksrotāstu yaḥ proktaḥ stairyagyonyastataḥ smṛtaḥ //
20.d:
मुख्यः सर्गश् चतुर्थस्तु मुख्या वै स्थावराः स्मृताः /
तिर्यक्स्रोतास्तु यः प्रोक्तः स्तैर्यग्योन्यस्ततः स्मृतः //
20.m: The fourth creation is the primary; the immobile beings are known as the primary. / That which is proclaimed as having an oblique flow of life is remembered as that of the animals.

20.s:
tathordhvasrotasāṃ ṣaṣṭho devasargastu sa smṛtaḥ /
tatorvāksrotasāṃ sargaḥ saptamaḥ sa tu mānuṣaḥ //
20.d:
तथोर्ध्वस्रोतसां षष्ठो देवसर्गस्तु स स्मृतः /
ततोर्वाक्स्रोतसां सर्गः सप्तमः स तु मानुषः //
20.m: Likewise, the sixth, that of beings with an upward flow of life, is known as the creation of the gods; / then the seventh creation, of beings with a downward flow of life, is that of humans.

20.s:
aṣṭamonugrahaḥ sargaiḥ sātvikastāmasaś ca yaḥ /
pañcaite vaikṛtāḥ sargāḥ prākṛtāś ca trayaḥ smṛtāḥ //
20.d:
अष्टमोनुग्रहः सर्गैः सात्विकस्तामसश् च यः /
पञ्चैते वैकृताः सर्गाः प्राकृताश् च त्रयः स्मृताः //
20.m: The eighth is the benevolent creation, which is characterised by goodness and darkness. / These five are secondary creations, and three are known as primary.

20.s:
prākṛto vaikṛtaś caiva kaumāro navamas tathā /
:p 50
brahmato nava sargāstu jagato mūlahetavaḥ //
20.d:
प्राकृतो वैकृतश् चैव कौमारो नवमस् तथा /
:प् 50
ब्रह्मतो नव सर्गास्तु जगतो मूलहेतवः //
20.m:
The ninth is the Kaumāra creation, both primary and secondary.
[Page 50]
These are the nine creations from Brahmā, the root causes of the universe.

20.s:
khyātyādyā dakṣakanyāstu bhṛgvādyā upayemire /
nityo naimittakaḥ sargastridhā prakathito janaiḥ //
20.d:
ख्यात्याद्या दक्षकन्यास्तु भृग्वाद्या उपयेमिरे /
नित्यो नैमित्तकः सर्गस्त्रिधा प्रकथितो जनैः //
20.m: Khyāti and other daughters of Dakṣa were married by Bhṛgu and others. / Creation is described by people as threefold: perpetual, occasional, [and causal].

20.s:
prākṛtā dainandinī syādantarapralayādanu /
jāyate yatrānudinaṃ mityasargo hi sammataḥ //
20.d:
प्राकृता दैनन्दिनी स्यादन्तरप्रलयादनु /
जायते यत्रानुदिनं मित्यसर्गो हि सम्मतः //
20.m: The elemental [dissolution] and the daily [dissolution] occur after an intermediate dissolution; / that creation which takes place daily is considered the perpetual creation.

20.s:
devau dhātāvidhātārau bhṛgoḥ khyātirasūyata /
śriyañca patnī viṣṇoryā stutā śakreṇa vṛddhaye //
20.d:
देवौ धाताविधातारौ भृगोः ख्यातिरसूयत /
श्रियञ्च पत्नी विष्णोर्या स्तुता शक्रेण वृद्धये //
20.m: Khyāti bore to Bhṛgu two gods, Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, / and Śrī, who is the consort of Viṣṇu, praised by Śakra for prosperity.

20.s:
dhāturvidhārturdvau putrau kramāt prāṇo mṛkaṇḍukaḥ /
mārkaṇḍeyo mṛkaṇḍoś ca jajñe vedaśirāstataḥ //
20.d:
धातुर्विधार्तुर्द्वौ पुत्रौ क्रमात् प्राणो मृकण्डुकः /
मार्कण्डेयो मृकण्डोश् च जज्ञे वेदशिरास्ततः //
20.m: To Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ were born two sons respectively, Prāṇa and Mṛkaṇḍu; / from Mṛkaṇḍu was born Mārkaṇḍeya, and from him Vedaśiras.

20.s:
paurṇamāsaś ca sambhūtyāṃ marīcerabhavat sutaḥ /
smṛtyāmaṅgirasaḥ putrāḥ sinīvālī kuhūs tathā //
20.d:
पौर्णमासश् च सम्भूत्यां मरीचेरभवत् सुतः /
स्मृत्यामङ्गिरसः पुत्राः सिनीवाली कुहूस् तथा //
20.m: And Paurṇamāsa was the son of Marīci through Sambhūti. / Through Smṛti, Aṅgiras had sons, and Sinīvālī and Kuhū,

20.s:
rākāścānumatiścātreranasūyāpyajījanat /
somaṃ durvāsasaṃ putraṃ dattātreyañca yoginam //
20.d:
राकाश्चानुमतिश्चात्रेरनसूयाप्यजीजनत् /
सोमं दुर्वाससं पुत्रं दत्तात्रेयञ्च योगिनम् //
20.m: as well as Rākā and Anumati. Through Anasūyā, Atri also fathered / Soma, the son Durvāsas, and the yogin Dattātreya.

20.s:
prītyāṃ pulastyabhāryāyāṃ dattolistatsutobhavat /
kṣamāyāṃ(1) pulahājjātāḥ sahiṣṇuḥ karmapādikāḥ //
20.d:
प्रीत्यां पुलस्त्यभार्यायां दत्तोलिस्तत्सुतोभवत् /
क्षमायां(1) पुलहाज्जाताः सहिष्णुः कर्मपादिकाः //
20.m: Through Prīti, wife of Pulastya, Dattoli was his son. / Through Kṣamā, from Pulaha were born Sahiṣṇu, Karmapāda, and the rest.

20.s:
sannatyāñca kratorāsan bālikhilyā mahaujasaḥ /
aṅguṣṭhaparvamātrāste ye hi ṣaṣṭisahasviṇaḥ //
20.d:
सन्नत्याञ्च क्रतोरासन् बालिखिल्या महौजसः /
अङ्गुष्ठपर्वमात्रास्ते ये हि षष्टिसहस्विणः //
20.m: And through Sannati, Kratu had the Vālikhilyas of great splendor; / they are merely the size of a thumb-joint, sixty thousand in number.

20.s:
urjāyāñca vaśiṣṭhācca rājā gātrordhvabāhukaḥ(2) /
savanaścālaghuḥ śukraḥ(3) sutapāḥ sapta carṣayaḥ //
20.d:
उर्जायाञ्च वशिष्ठाच्च राजा गात्रोर्ध्वबाहुकः(2) /
सवनश्चालघुः शुक्रः(3) सुतपाः सप्त चर्षयः //
20.m: And through Ūrjā, from Vasiṣṭha came Rāja, Gātra, Ūrdhvabāhu, / Savana, Anagha, Śukra, and Sutapas—the seven ṛṣis.

20.s:
pāvakaḥ pavamānobhūcchuciḥ svāhāgnijobhavat /
:n
1 kumāryāmiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 rajogotrordhvāhuka iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ rājā
śātrordhvabālaka iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ, rajogotrordhvavāhaka iti
ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 sabalaścānaghaḥ śukra iti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 51
agnisvāttā varhiṣado 'nagnayaḥ sāgnayo hy ajāt(1) //
20.d:
पावकः पवमानोभूच्छुचिः स्वाहाग्निजोभवत् /
:न्
1 कुमार्यामिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 रजोगोत्रोर्ध्वाहुक इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः राजा
शात्रोर्ध्वबालक इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः, रजोगोत्रोर्ध्ववाहक इति
ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 सबलश्चानघः शुक्र इति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 51
अग्निस्वात्ता वर्हिषदो ऽनग्नयः साग्नयो ह्य् अजात्(1) //
20.m:
Pāvaka, Pavamāna, and Śuci were born of Agni and Svāhā.
[Footnote]
1. "kumāryām" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2. "rajogotrordhvāhukaḥ" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha; "rājā śātrordhvabālakaḥ" in ga; "rajogotrordhvavāhakaḥ" in ṅa.
3. "sabalaścānaghaḥ śukraḥ" is the reading in the manuscript marked gha. / [p. 51]
The Agniṣvāttas and Barhiṣads, without sacred fires and with sacred fires, were born [of Brahmā].

20.s:
pitṛbhyaś ca svadhāyāñca menā vaidhāriṇī sute(2) /
hiṃsābhāryā tvadharmasya tayorjajñe tathānṛtam //
20.d:
पितृभ्यश् च स्वधायाञ्च मेना वैधारिणी सुते(2) /
हिंसाभार्या त्वधर्मस्य तयोर्जज्ञे तथानृतम् //
20.m: And from the Pitṛs through Svadhā were born two daughters, Menā and Vaidhāriṇī. / But Hiṃsā was the wife of Adharma; to the two of them was born Anṛta,

20.s:
kanyā ca nikṛtistābhyāṃ bhayannarakemeva ca /
māyā ca vedanā caiva mithunantvidametayoḥ //
20.d:
कन्या च निकृतिस्ताभ्यां भयन्नरकेमेव च /
माया च वेदना चैव मिथुनन्त्विदमेतयोः //
20.m: and the maiden Nikṛti; from those two came Bhaya and Naraka, / and Māyā and Vedanā; this indeed is the pair born of these two.

20.s:
tayorjajñetha vai māyāṃ mṛtyuṃ bhūtāpahāriṇam /
vedanā ca sutaṃ cāpi duḥkhaṃ jajñetha rauravāt //
20.d:
तयोर्जज्ञेथ वै मायां मृत्युं भूतापहारिणम् /
वेदना च सुतं चापि दुःखं जज्ञेथ रौरवात् //
20.m: Then to those two was born Māyā; [and] Mṛtyu, who carries off living beings; / and Vedanā bore a son, Duḥkha, from Raurava.

20.s:
mṛtyorvyādhijarāśokatṛṣṇākrodhāś ca jajñire /
brahmaṇaś ca rudan jāto rodanādrudranāmakaḥ //
20.d:
मृत्योर्व्याधिजराशोकतृष्णाक्रोधाश् च जज्ञिरे /
ब्रह्मणश् च रुदन् जातो रोदनाद्रुद्रनामकः //
20.m: From Mṛtyu were born Vyādhi, Jarā, Śoka, Tṛṣṇā, and Krodha. / And from Brahmā, weeping, was born [a son] who was called Rudra because of his crying.

20.s:
bhavaṃ śarvamatheśānaṃ tathā paśupatiṃ dvija /
bhīmamugraṃ mahādevamuvāca sa pitāmahaḥ //
20.d:
भवं शर्वमथेशानं तथा पशुपतिं द्विज /
भीममुग्रं महादेवमुवाच स पितामहः //
20.m: The Grandfather spoke to him as Bhava, Śarva, then Īśāna, / and Paśupati, O twice-born, and Bhīma, Ugra, and Mahādeva.

20.s:
dakṣakopācca tadbhāryā dehantatyāja sā satī /
himavadduhitā bhūtvā patnī śambhorabhūt punaḥ //
20.d:
दक्षकोपाच्च तद्भार्या देहन्तत्याज सा सती /
हिमवद्दुहिता भूत्वा पत्नी शम्भोरभूत् पुनः //
20.m: And out of wrath at Dakṣa, his wife Satī abandoned her body; / becoming the daughter of Himavat, she again became the wife of Śambhu.

20.s:
ṛṣibhyo nāradādyuktāḥ pūjāḥ snānādipūrvikāḥ /
svāyambhuvādyāstāḥ kṛtvā viṣṇvāderbhuktimuktidāḥ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye jagatsargavarṇanaṃ nāma viṃśatitamo
'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha ekaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
sāmānyapūjākathanaṃ
20.d:
ऋषिभ्यो नारदाद्युक्ताः पूजाः स्नानादिपूर्विकाः /
स्वायम्भुवाद्यास्ताः कृत्वा विष्ण्वादेर्भुक्तिमुक्तिदाः //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये जगत्सर्गवर्णनं नाम विंशतितमो
ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ एकविंशो ऽध्यायः
सामान्यपूजाकथनं
20.m:
The rites of worship preceded by bathing and the like, spoken of by Nārada and others to the ṛṣis, / having been performed by Svāyambhuva and others, bestow worldly enjoyment and liberation with respect to Viṣṇu and others.
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, named "Description of the Creation of the Universe," in the venerable Agni Mahāpurāṇa.
Now, the twenty-first chapter.
Instruction on General Worship
